props.title: Sam LaPorta OVER 4.5 receptions
props.cutoff: OVER 4.5 at +100 or better. Pass at 5.5 or any minus price; reverify after quote expiry.
props.edge: Original 53% judgment is uncalibrated and is not supported strongly enough by the evening comparison to renew. At +101, break-even is 49.75%; the cited 46% provider estimate would imply negative value, but that model also lacks established calibration. No positive current edge claimed. Original projection 4.9 and original quote +116 are retained for later evaluation.
props.why: The original recommendation used 4.9 expected catches. The evening comparison found LineupExperts 4.6, StatIQ 4.2 and MatchWiz 4.8; MatchWiz estimates only 46% to exceed 4.5 and warns about model performance. These are not equally calibrated models or a consensus probability. A mean above 4.5 does not establish a profitable five-catch bet. New entries are paused; the original decision remains on the record.
props.risk: His fifth Week 1 catch came in overtime; regulation was four catches for 39 yards. Most historical games precede his 2025 back injury and coordinator change. Missing Detroit linemen could create extra pass-blocking assignments, while St. Brown, Williams and Gibbs compete for targets. Routes remain unverified. This shares Detroit passing-volume exposure with the earlier Gibbs play, so they are not independent parlay legs.

props.title: Jahmyr Gibbs OVER 29.5 receiving yards
props.cutoff: OVER 29.5 at -115 or better only; pass at 30.5+ or -116 and worse. Reverify the live price after expiry.
props.edge: Projected mean +3.5 yards, not a probability edge. Uncalibrated judgment: about 55% to clear, versus 53.49% break-even at -115 (about +1.5 percentage points; about +2.8% expected return if that estimate is right). Plausible 50–60% uncertainty includes negative value.
props.why: The verified 29.5-yard number is below his 34.4 last-five and 44.9 last-ten averages. Five targets and 30 receiving yards in Week 1 support continuing receiving involvement; the team confirms an expanded lead-back role. My conservative 33-yard projection uses 5.5 targets × 75% catches × 8 yards per catch, below the recent target averages. Buffalo favored by 5.5 gives a plausible passing script. Detroit line absences may encourage outlets, but that is an inference, not the main reason.
props.risk: Thin estimated edge and uncertain routes under a new coordinator. Missing Mahogany and Miller could require Gibbs to block instead. Buffalo held Houston RBs to four catches for 17 yards last week; that one game does not prove a favorable matchup. Overtime inflated Week 1 touches. Inactives and wind remain pregame checks; no unsupported weather or scheme boost.

parlays.risk: Kincaid four catches is the weakest historical leg; his five-catch opener does not prove a stable new role. Cook had only 13 carries for 57 yards last week. parlays.edge: No demonstrated positive EV and no calibrated joint probability. +360 requires 21.74% to break even; no claim is made that this ticket exceeds that. It returns +3.6u profit and 4.6u total only if every leg wins at the recorded price. Individual historical rates are not multiplied. This is deliberately separate from favorites and their returns.
parlays.correlation: All legs share one game’s pace and script. Cook rushing can trade off with Buffalo passing volume. Gibbs and LaPorta compete for Detroit targets. These dependencies can help or hurt; +360 is the actual offered combined sportsbook price, never a product of single-leg odds. It also repeats exposure to the earlier Gibbs and LaPorta straight selections; this is intentional entertainment overlap, not diversification.

takeaways: Sep 17 final: Gibbs had 61 receiving yards against the unchanged 33-yard projection; LaPorta had six catches against 4.9. Both won at their original lines. The evening entry pauses are retained, not rewritten after the wins.

The +360 fun SGP cleared all four legs: Cook 135 rushing yards, Gibbs 61 receiving yards, Kincaid seven catches and LaPorta six. It remains a high-risk speculative ticket; one win does not establish positive expected value.

Bills 41-31: the frozen elo-total-v1 baseline was Buffalo 28-23. Winner correct; total 51 versus actual 72, a 21-point miss, and home margin +5 versus +10, a five-point miss. Score accuracy stays separate from the betting record.

Buffalo confirmed a pregame hip injury for Ed Oliver and an in-game shoulder/stinger exit for DJ Moore. These personnel changes belong in the next matchup and workload review; they do not prove why a pregame price moved.
weeklyReview: NFL Week 2, judgment-volume-v1, two straight props from one game: original projections minus actuals were -28 receiving yards for Gibbs and -1.1 receptions for LaPorta. Keep these different stat units separate; do not average them into a single error score.

Gibbs workload decomposition: original assumption 5.5 targets x 75% catches x 8 yards per catch; actual eight targets x 75% catches x 10.17 yards per catch = 61 yards. Both opportunity and efficiency exceeded the assumptions. This trailing-game sample alone cannot justify raising future projections.

Hypothesis retained: receptions require a distribution around expected volume, not a mean-only edge. LaPorta winning does not validate the uncalibrated 53% probability or invalidate the evening caution. Compare later games without changing original forecasts.

New review hypothesis, registered after this game: receiving workload comparisons should flag meaningful in-game teammate exits before treating target changes as a stable role. Test on later games with confirmed participation and route data; no model change or improved-accuracy claim today.
No genuine pregame closing observation was recorded. The 17:34 ET snapshots remain earlier price observations, not closing-line value.
